patch_description: The random configuration gives essentially zero ratio. A good structure for this problem is points on a sphere (which fixes dmax near the diameter for antipodal-ish spreads, and normalizing lets the ratio equal dmin/dmax of the unit-sphere configuration). I optimize a Tammes-like problem: place 14 points on the unit sphere maximizing the minimum pairwise distance, using a smooth soft-min surrogate (logsumexp with decreasing temperature) minimized with L-BFGS-B, from several fixed-seed restarts. The configuration with the best actual dmin/dmax ratio is returned. This is the known best approach for such "max-min / min-max" point-spreading problems and should reach a squared ratio near the reference ~1/4.166 (ratio ≈ 0.49, achieved by the optimal 14-point spherical arrangement with several antipodal pairs).
